system_overview: The Invoice API lets customer finance users and partner systems read invoices, export them as CSV files, receive status webhooks and request refunds. It is a Node.js service behind a public REST API, backed by a PostgreSQL database, with background workers for exports and webhooks and a separate payments service for refunds.

This review supports the decision to open the API to partners. It found three weaknesses evidenced in code and two design hypotheses. The most significant is that bulk exports are not authorised per invoice, and the export worker reads with an all-tenant service role.

key_components.name: Export worker
key_components.why: Runs with a service role that can read every tenant's invoices, so any gap in export authorisation exposes data across users.

key_components.name: Invoice API
key_components.why: Enforces tenant membership but not per-user ownership on invoice reads and export requests.

key_components.name: Webhook dispatcher
key_components.why: Makes outbound calls from inside the application network to customer-chosen addresses and follows redirects.

key_components.name: Payments and refunds service
key_components.why: Moves money; its duplicate-request protection has not been fully traced.

next_steps.step: Authorise every invoice in an export against the requesting user, at request time and again in the worker.
Decide the intended invoice visibility within a tenant, then bind reads to the owner or an explicit grant.
Validate webhook destinations at send time and stop following redirects to private addresses.
Confirm partner credential scopes before partner onboarding begins.
Run the four planned verification tests in an isolated environment.

approach: We reviewed the invoice platform's source code and infrastructure definitions alongside its architecture documentation, and confirmed our understanding of the components, data flows and trust boundaries with the client's engineers in workshops.

From that we identified what could go wrong at each component and flow, recorded the controls already in place, and proposed recommendations and verification tests. Threats were classified with STRIDE and mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and CAPEC where the behaviour was specific enough. Risks were rated with the client using the matrix in Appendix C.

activities.description: Agreed the decision the review supports, the in-scope components and exclusions.
Review of source code, infrastructure definitions and design documentation.
System model, trust boundaries, threats, existing controls and gaps.
Likelihood and consequence agreed with the client for each rateable threat.
Recommendations, verification plans and this report.

review_coverage: The API routes, authentication middleware, export worker, webhook dispatcher and storage definitions were reviewed in full. The payments settlement client and the admin console were not reviewed.
limitations: This was a time-boxed review of the design and code; no testing was performed against a running system.
The payments settlement integration was not reviewed, so the assessment of the payments service is partial.
Findings reflect the code at the reviewed revision and the documentation supplied.
